claim: Purpose is the preset a director sets before touching anything else: it decides how big the subject sits in the frame and what the frame is actually about. Reach for it when you want the shot to do a job - plant the location, land a face, hold a beat - instead of hand-dialling size, lens and duration one at a time.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: wide shot, scenery, full body, distant subject
backlighting, emerging from shadow, dramatic entrance
blurry, motion blur, out of focus

review.issue: detail ("extreme close-up, cropped, object focus") and insert ("close-up, soccer ball, object focus") share the same tag core, and in a soccer scene the detail panel will almost certainly land on the ball too — two options, one picture. reveal ("emerging from shadow, dramatic entrance") and mood ("atmospheric, ambient light") are description rather than danbooru tags: none of those four phrases are trained, so those panels rest entirely on "backlighting" and "looking away".
review.fix: Anchor detail on something else the subject sentence already contains — "extreme close-up, jersey number, fabric texture" — and let insert own the ball. Rewrite reveal as "backlighting, silhouette, rim lighting" and mood as "dark, dramatic shadow, looking away", which are all trained tags.
